newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan money rise shows gradual recovery-economists.
newsitem.headline: Japan money rise shows gradual recovery-economists.

text.p: Growth of 3.7 percent in Japan's money supply in October shows that the economy is continuing to recover gradually, economists said on Tuesday.

The Bank of Japan said earlier on Tuesday that Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (CDs), a key gauge of money supply, grew a preliminary 3.7 percent year-on-year in October, compared with a revised 3.5 percent rise in September.
"The money supply growth reflects the economy's gradual recovery trend," said Mamoru Yamaguchi, an economist for Nikko Research Center.
Satoru Kado, a senior economist at Sanwa Research Institute, said the October figures showed money supply growth was still not very strong.
"I do not think money supply growth will increase substantially in the coming months," Kado said.
Money supply growth was unlikely to increase in the near future, unless fund demand from small- and medium-sized firms increased, Kado said.
Nikko's Yamaguchi said bank lending and consumption needed to increase, if the economic recovery was to gain more momentum. -- Tokyo Treasury Desk, +81-3-5473-3748
